study.title: Python Remediation Experiment - Eight-Problem Template
study.description: Three-condition, individually randomized experiment comparing additional practice, similar worked examples, and matched worked examples after incorrect Python code-writing submissions.
study.notes:
APPROVED MATERIAL MAPPING (2026-10-29): Q09-Q16 in numeric order, paired respectively with M01-M04 then H01-H04 for additional practice. Quinn approved this ordering and pairing on 2026-10-29. The new bank has 28 activities (8 Q originals + 20 M/H variants), superseding the earlier 20-item bank description. Twelve M05-M10/H05-H10 variants remain unassigned; they are not automatically used as pretest or final-test questions.
16 Cupcake SPLICE delivery URLs and catalog identities are populated. All 24 condition-specific failure rules remain connected. Similar-example and matched-example targets still need real worked-example URLs; do not use free-coding activities in those conditions. Proposed similar examples should explain the paired practice problem; matched examples must explain the original solution line by line. No corresponding study WEAT records were identified in the public catalog of 4,130 entries on 2026-10-29.
Pairing caveats: M03 uses equality instead of >=; H02 adds a second update in the else branch; H04 changes the second comparison and executes both updates. Other pairs also change boundary/outcome cases. These differences are documented for the research team; the owner approved the pairings.
All 28 catalog reference programs match their declared stdout locally. Most activities have one visible fixed-output test; M09 has an additional hidden test. This does not certify live provider callbacks or establish that output matching assesses code structure. Pilot real wrong/correct submissions before recruitment.

CONFIGURATION TEMPLATE - replace materials before recruitment.
Eight learning slots now use the proposed Q09-Q16 mapping above. For each slot, replace the existing Smart Content URL/metadata in place; do not delete and recreate the activity, because branch rules reference its database identity. Each slot has one additional-practice, one similar-example, and one matched-example target. Practice candidates come from the remaining twelve bank items; selection/reuse is not specified. Match knowledge components; matched examples must explain the exact original solution line by line. Neutral activity titles preserve condition blinding.
FLOW: consent -> baseline measures -> pretest -> eight learning problems -> post-session questionnaire -> two randomized transfer questions -> debrief -> recruitment completion. All three conditions share the main sequence. Incorrect -> assigned remediation -> original retry. Correct -> next learning problem. Additional practice returns after one scored submission, correct or incorrect; examples return on completion. Further errors on the original repeat remediation: confirm this stopping policy before launch. No ordinary optional recommendation sidebar is used.
REPLACE: approved consent/eligibility and decline/withdrawal instructions; indices.docx wording and validated response scales; baseline/pretest items and experience measure; all 16 worked-example URLs; final two transfer questions and rubric.docx; debrief; Prolific study/completion codes. No URLs or question solutions are invented. The 16 worked-example slots cannot run until URLs are supplied. Final native text responses are stored for rubric scoring; form completion scores are not test-performance scores.
TIMING: all section limits are 0 (untimed); the estimated 30-minute visit does not specify hard section deadlines. Set only approved limits. Original learning-section timer includes remediation time.
PROLIFIC: independent random assignment across three active conditions; US adults 18+, $6, approximately 30 minutes, target 300 qualifying completers (about 100 per condition). Configure eligibility/payment externally. No entry cap is used as a substitute for qualifying-completer count. Recruitment is disabled and completion codes blank.
MEASUREMENT: preserve event scores, incorrect attempts, transitions, raw timestamps and input summaries. Native text inputs record keystroke/copy/paste counts; external providers require their own telemetry. Review evidence, do not automatically classify cheating. Exclusions, rubric scoring, winsorization and regression are researcher analyses. Second-order confidence items use 0-10 choices. Final transfer-question order is shuffled once per participant and stable on revisit.
BANK AUDIT: Q04 prints 15.0 in Python 3; Q16 has a second if without else. Confirm expected outputs with provider authors.
